Closes #18337

## To test:

**Prerequisites:** [See this PR](https://github.com/wordpress-mobile/WordPress-iOS/pull/18298) for instructions on enabling the Site Name feature.

_Please note: If testing this PR via Xcode, you can verify Tracks events via the Xcode log. If you're testing this on a PR build or a beta build of the app, you can either use the Tracks dashboard or the in-app logs (tap profile pic → "Help and Support" → "Activity Logs")._

**Important**: If you're overriding the experiment variants manually, don't be surprised if the event value doesn't match what you'd expect (e.g. it shows `control` though you can see the view). This is dependent on where you overrode the value.

1. Start Site Creation flow
2. Expect three events: `enhanced_site_creation_intent_question_experiment`, `enhanced_site_creation_site_name_experiment`, `enhanced_site_creation_accessed`, `enhanced_site_creation_intent_question_viewed`
3. Tap a vertical
4. Expect two events: `enhanced_site_creation_intent_question_vertical_selected`, `enhanced_site_creation_site_name_viewed`
5. Tap "Skip" at the top right on the Site Name screen
6. Expect two events: `enhanced_site_creation_site_name_skipped`, `enhanced_site_creation_site_design_viewed`
7. Tap the back arrow at the top left on the Design Screen (as of this PR the text for Site Name isn't showing in the nav bar, this will be fixed)
8. Tap the back arrow at the top left on the Site Name screen
9. Expect one event `enhanced_site_creation_site_name_canceled`
10. Tap a vertical (events from step 4 will fire again)
11. Type a site name and tap "Continue"
12. Expect one event `enhanced_site_creation_site_name_entered` with a property `site_name` containing the name that was typed in step 11

## Regression Notes
1. Potential unintended areas of impact
- Sending Tracks events during Site Creation

2. What I did to test those areas of impact (or what existing automated tests I relied on)
- Tested manually with the steps above
- Ran existing automated tests related to Site Creation

3. What automated tests I added (or what prevented me from doing so)

body:
Problem
=======
Dependabot alerts were bugging me like crazy.

Solution
========
`markdown-spellchecker` is the package that depends on outdated & insecure versions of `marked`, and it appears to be no longer maintained.  I searched a bit for an alternative and found one that is actively maintained, [`yaspeller`](https://github.com/hcodes/yaspeller).

Some advantages of yaspeller:
You can tell it to ignore any words with numbers in them, words with all uppercase, and its custom dictionary also accepts regular expressions. This made our dictionary a lot smaller.  It also uses a config file.

- [x] install yaspeller and uninstall markdown-spellcheker

- [x] make sure tests/CI still pass

### What I did
fix an optimization heuristic in copy_bytes. when `length_bound` is 0, a load and store can be generated even when the destination has 0 bytes allocated for it. the bug was introduced in #2653.

fixes #2773.

### How I did it
don't copy any bytes when `length_bound` is 0.

### How to verify it
check the tests. note that in the tests, I hardcoded the ABI encoding of the empty string since eth-abi generates extra padding bytes (cf. https://github.com/ethereum/eth-abi/issues/157).

author: gosar
body:
After 1.19.0, we released a release candidate 1.21.0-rc1 for testing a release candidate that we didn't expect to get used generally.

But the [Gradle plugin](https://github.com/awslabs/smithy-gradle-plugin/blob/main/build.gradle.kts#L32-L34) currently uses
```
    implementation("software.amazon.smithy:smithy-model:[1.0, 2.0[")
    implementation("software.amazon.smithy:smithy-build:[1.0, 2.0[")
    implementation("software.amazon.smithy:smithy-cli:[1.0, 2.0[")
```
which based on Gradle ordering rules, finds 1.21.0-rc1, which caused issues to existing customers, like https://github.com/awslabs/smithy/issues/1186

Releasing 1.21.0 will fix the issues as, 1.21.0 will be picked over 1.21.0-rc1. So we are skipping 1.20.0.

When user logs in they will be forcefully redirected to complete their profile which includes setting their: email, first name, and last name.

If they already have an existing pennsieve account then we will authenticate them and link their orcid account to their pennsieve account.

author: naps62
body:
Partial withdrawals are necessary when users want to withdraw, but there isn't enough liquidity in the vault. This can happen for multiple reasons, namely:

1. The withdrawal is bigger than the non-investable percentage. For instance, if the vault invests 95% of the funds and the withdrawals, but the deposit represents 6%.
2. Someone has already withdrawn from the vault, and it has not yet rebalanced with the strategy.

A new external function is introduced, taking in a list of ids and a list of amounts. The idea is to delegate to the caller the responsibility of choosing the deposits to withdraw from.

Say Alice deposits 100 UST and assigns 30% of the yield to Bob and 70% to Carol. She may then want to do either of the following:

* do a partial withdrawal of 70 UST, all from Carol's share, leaving only Bob's share
* do a proportional withdrawal from each of them (70 * 0.7 from Carol and 70 * 0.3 from Bob)
* do some other combination of values that amounts to 70 UST

In this way, we can choose any of these approaches on the UI and iterate later on.

### Async withdrawals

This removes the need to implement async withdrawals, which are more complex (both technically and UX-wise).
If a user owns more than 5% of a vault, he would now be able to make a partial withdrawal of that 5% immediately instead of requesting an async withdrawal. This would also give us time to intervene if needed, should a bank run occur and allow us to increase the liquidity available in the vault to respond to all intended withdrawals.

### Force withdraws

The vault also has a force feature that allows users to withdraw at a loss (e.g., a black swan event that causes a negative yield). To avoid writing a mess of code, partial withdrawals are not allowed during loss scenarios, only full withdrawals with force.

author: leah-splitkb
body:
## Description

QMK currently has excellent support for encoder attached directly to the MCU.
In some cases it may not be possible to attach them directly so it is desirable to use, say, and IO expander.

Just like the custom matrix code does for the matrix, this PR aims to make it possible to provide custom hardware-specific code for reading out the encoders.

Default behaviour is unchanged, but setting `CUSTOM_ENCODER = yes` adds two new hooks:
```c
void encoder_init_pads(uint8_t count, bool pads[]);
void encoder_read_pads(uint8_t count, bool pads[]);
```
The former is used to initialize whatever hardware is used to read the encoders and read the initial state, the latter is used to get subsequent updates.

### Possible points of discussion
- **Does `count` need to be passed?** On `master`, both halves of a split keyboard feature the same number of encoders, so the callee could just use `NUMBER_OF_ENCODERS`. However, `develop` made it possible to have a different number of encoders per side, making it more likely that an implementer will use that instead of the per-half encoder count. Explicitly providing the encoder count here makes this less likely.
-  **Why bool arrays?** The callee most probably reads the value per-pin, so having a 2-tuple of booleans representing pin state feels like the most natural format. We could pass it as a per-encoder `uint8_t` instead like the underlying code uses, but as the array is immediately discarded it provides zero memory benefit while making the API less obvious.
-  **Does `init` need to read the pads?** Theoretically, no. However, unlike the key matrix, the encoder code *must* know the initial state of the encoders during initialization - but the keyboard is in an "abnormal" state and may not behave exactly as it does during a regular read. Keeping track of first vs. subsequent reads in `encoder_read_pads` itself is rather painful, so I believe it is best to have the first read occur as part of the initialization. In cases where the keyboard state does not matter, calling `read` at the end of `init` is trivial anyways.

### Potential future work
This code simply provides ways to replace the use of `readPin` in encoder code, but it still assumes the use of EC11-like encoders. As such, it is more of a `CUSTOM_ENCODER = lite`.
It might be useful in the future to further abstract the encoder code away from hardware details, allowing the use of devices like scroll wheels, analog dials, or other rotary-like gadgets by directly providing `encoder_value`. However, that would require a significant rewrite and as such is currently considered to be out of scope.

## What is this change?

Adds the `etcd-unsafe-no-fsync` backend configuration option ("disables fsync, unsafe, may cause data loss").

This makes it possible to run a sensu-backend with an embedded etcd node for testing and development without placing lots of load on the file system.

## Why is this change necessary?

Local disk/storage may not perform well enough for etcd.

body: Snowfakery's integration testing infrastructure is based on CumulusCI's. CumulusCI's now depends on client apps declaring the `salesforce_serializer`. This PR declares a `salesforce_serializer` which is just the default VCR serializer. Snowfakery doesn't need the compressed serializer yet.

   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.21.37
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``mediaconvert``: [``botocore``] AWS Elemental MediaConvert SDK has added support for the pass-through of WebVTT styling to WebVTT outputs, pass-through of KLV metadata to supported formats, and improved filter support for processing 444/RGB content.

* api-change:``pi``: [``botocore``] Adds support for DocumentDB to the Performance Insights API.
* api-change:``events``: [``botocore``] Update events client to latest version
* api-change:``docdb``: [``botocore``] Added support to enable/disable performance insights when creating or modifying db instances

   ### 1.21.35

   ### 1.21.34
   ```
   =======

   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.21.33
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``sms``: [``botocore``] Revised product update notice for SMS console deprecation.
* api-change:``proton``: [``botocore``] SDK release to support tagging for AWS Proton Repository resource
* enhancement:AWSCRT: [``botocore``] Upgrade awscrt version to 0.13.8
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.21.32
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``connect``: [``botocore``] This release updates these APIs: UpdateInstanceAttribute, DescribeInstanceAttribute and ListInstanceAttributes.    ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.21.31
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``cloudcontrol``: [``botocore``] SDK release for Cloud Control API in Amazon Web Services China (Beijing) Region, operated by Sinnet, and Amazon Web Services China (Ningxia) Region, operated by NWCD
* api-change:``pinpoint-sms-voice-v2``: [``botocore``] Amazon Pinpoint now offers a version 2.0 suite of SMS and voice APIs, providing increased control over sending and configuration. This release is a new SDK for sending SMS and voice messages called PinpointSMSVoiceV2.
* api-change:``workspaces``: [``botocore``] Added APIs that allow you to customize the logo, login message, and help links in the WorkSpaces client login page. To learn more, visit https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/customize-branding.html
* api-change:``route53-recovery-cluster``: [``botocore``] This release adds a new API "ListRoutingControls" to list routing control states using the highly reliable Route 53 ARC data plane endpoints.
* api-change:``databrew``: [``botocore``] This AWS Glue Databrew release adds feature to support ORC as an input format.
* api-change:``auditmanager``: [``botocore``] This release adds documentation updates for Audit Manager. The updates provide data deletion guidance when a customer deregisters Audit Manager or deregisters a delegated administrator.
* api-change:``grafana``: [``botocore``] This release adds tagging support to the Managed Grafana service. New APIs: TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource. Updates: add optional field tags to support tagging while calling CreateWorkspace.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 1.21.30
   ```
   =======

* api-change:``iot-data``: [``botocore``] Update the default AWS IoT Core Data Plane endpoint from VeriSign signed to ATS signed. If you have firewalls with strict egress rules, configure the rules to grant you access

This PR focuses on adding support for inheriting `include` and `exclude`. While they were not in the original RFC it was decided that they should be added per [epage's comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/8415#issuecomment-1097422198).

author: deepstqte
body:
The user experience for when the query doesn't return any results could be improved. Currently the shown results remain displayed and the console shows the error:

```
(index):253 Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'columns')
    at Loader.next ((index):253:35)
```

This is because when no results are returned, the `contents` array is empty in the following line

https://github.com/mixtape-network/mferbase/blob/4ec815a841baa951490d2079552f538a68c59cb3/index.html#L253

Here is an example of a query to reproduce this:

```
"chain" is not null
and "4:20 watch" is not null
and "hat under headphones" is not null
and "long hair" is not null
and "smoke" is not null
and "beard" is not null
and "shirt" is not null
```

This is also problematic since if there is a SQL error, the same thing happens, so in the case of "no results" it's not clear if there is a problem with the query or simply there were no results returned.

This PR does the following:

- Add a condition to check if the `contents` array is empty or not.
- If `contents` is empty then it assigns "No results" to the `html` var.
- If it's not empty it does what it currently does, i.e. construct the results table.

author: tomdlt
body:
This PR proposes to use (q3, q7) instead of (q1, q9) in the plots.

For some fast benchmarks, computational time can vary a lot between runs, and the log-plots are highly visually affected by some unfortunate outliers. Using quantiles closer to the median would alleviate this issue by providing a more robust estimate of the computational times.

In a Gaussian distribution with zero-mean and unit standard deviation, the range [-0.5, 0.5] corresponds to the percentiles [30.8, 69.2], so the range (q3, q7) does seem a reasonable choice to me.

WDYT?

author: pedrohbraga
body:
Hi!

This pull request contains the translation of the changes I performed to the first part of the presentation. These changes are described in pull request #15.

In summary,  these changes address important issues with linearity and clarity that had been already raised by presenters and participants in this workshop. Most changes happened between the beginning and the hierarchical clustering methods part.

This update introduces simple concepts of matrix algebra. The material progressively builds on matrices and association matrices to then integrate a few commonly used distance coefficients and data transformation practices before the discussion about hierarchical clustering methods. 

There is now more written text, which will help guide both presenters and participants through the material.

I also added a new challenge, cleaned the presentation and added presenter notes.

I am tagging the current presenters for this workshop to allow them to decide whether they want to incorporate these changes prior to their presentation.

body: The "Skip to events" toggle seemed like a translation issue for me. The rrweb player isn't really skipping or jumping ahead when the video is idle, instead it's increasing the playback speed until there's something to show. Fast-forward I thought that this is something worth calling out on the UI, because the fast-forward speed that rrweb picks is variable, I've seen 4x and also 29x speeds in examples. This replaces the BooleanField with a togglable Button (could use a better icon). I don't think it's the best design, but chose it because a) No label: "Fast-forward through idle moments" seemed like a long label to display at all times b) I brought the icon into the Player frame. When the fast-forwarding happens you see the new speed, and the icon in the player matches the Button, because they're related. Test case was https://dev.getsentry.net:7999/organizations/sentry-emerging-tech/replays/sourcemapsio-replays:e0d1ef068d4b4aeca01d81b26ab2ad1f/
